summary: The original source supports a joint analysis of two CHI blocks numbered 5 and 6, intercepted on November 8. No earlier published reading matching the recovered wording was located. Norbert explicitly suggested a joint attack in 2017; this methodological priority is credited separately from the present recovery.

primary_source.title: General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System, Aegean Park Press collection of Childs material
primary_source.direction: The notation recipient v sender identifies CGH as the radio sender and FKR as the recipient. No station-to-unit identification is established.
primary_source.part_count_limit: Only the labels 5 TL and 6 TL are present. The source does not state a total count; describe these as parts 5 and 6 of a multipart message, or at least six parts.
primary_source.transcription_finding: The literal groups agree with the source catalog. Part 5 contains 132 valid coordinates. Part 6 contains 108 slots, including exactly 15 explicit dashes at zero-based indices 5 through 19.
primary_source.source_glyph_verdict: The fourth and fifth glyphs of AXVAA are clearly printed A and A. Changing either to X requires an explicit source emendation; it is not justified as correcting a modern visual transcription.
primary_source.missing_companions: No matching earlier or later part was identified in the whole-book header and ciphertext searches. This is a bounded negative search, not proof that no other copy survives elsewhere.

header_convention_evidence.title: German Military Ciphers from February to November 1918
header_convention_evidence.evidence: The prose identifies LP-to-COS traffic via NKJ and prints NKJ v LP; it identifies COS-to-OSM traffic and prints OSM v COS. These examples establish the direction convention used here.

CHI_scope_evidence.title: German Military Ciphers from February to November 1918
CHI_scope_evidence.finding: Childs distinguishes western CHI messages with daily key changes from eastern RICHI messages with multi-day key periods.
CHI_scope_evidence.limit: This is historical system-level context. It does not identify CGH or FKR, prove a specific formation, or rule out exceptional use of a CHI key in eastern traffic. The new reading must not automatically inherit the Balkan 11th Army setting of neighbouring RICHI material.

documented_exception.header: RVV v N4 (9.20 p.m., November 9th); 1750; CHI-242
documented_exception.finding: The source explicitly labels this eastern-route block CHI, although the independently established p158 component parallel decrypts with the RICHI November 7–9 key. Its label was visually rechecked. A CHI label alone does not prove the geographic origin or exact key family of every individual intercept.

prior_art.finding: The locally retrieved current page still lists both p153 CHI blocks as open; its known-key searches do not provide this reading.

comment_count_audit.secondary_file_observation: The extracted text has 55 line-start numbered records because comment 35 is merged into comment 34, followed by 15 unrelated recent-comment sidebar lines. It still contains all 56 numbered thread comments.
comment_count_audit.correction: Report 56 numbered comments reviewed. The sidebar entries are not additional ADFGVX thread contributions.

new_key_corpus_screen.method: Fixed recovered rank with the 19-cell body square, plus a separately labelled AF=X model; existing OCR group-length variants retained as explicit hypotheses.
new_key_corpus_screen.source_scope: Printed pages 57–230, with focused inspection of nearby CHI headers on printed pages 140–170.
new_key_corpus_screen.result: The two p153 blocks are the only coherent matches identified. No additional same-key companion was accepted.
new_key_corpus_screen.limitations: The unverified OCR may split, merge, omit or misread source blocks. This screen does not exclude a companion obscured by unmodelled transcription errors. No high-scoring random string was treated as plaintext.
new_key_corpus_screen.verification: Passed: 788 blocks, 10,896 fixed-key layout/square models, all-model SHA-256 34ae75827f4989f25fc5b48bd9168e142a63e13ab42ccb11593a5fcbb85ddb21.

call_sign_identification_limit.author: Phillip B. Whitehead
call_sign_identification_limit.title: Notes on the Liaison Service and the Liaison Intelligence Service of the German Army during the World War
call_sign_identification_limit.evidence: The primary report describes daily changes of call names from March 1918 and deliberate lateral traffic intended to obscure formation boundaries. Printed page 23 was visually checked.
call_sign_identification_limit.limit: This provides a general reason to require date-specific evidence before identifying CGH or FKR with a unit. It does not identify either call sign or establish the geographic origin of p153.

full_page_header_followup.result: The independently re-OCRed full intercept log retrieves the known p153 FKR/CGH header and 2250 field, but no additional matching part. Source-image inspection excludes the retrieved near-call-sign artifacts.
full_page_header_followup.limit: Complete OCR page coverage does not prove that a badly recognized or differently headed companion is absent.
